name: Funding Activity
blurb: Capital flowing into AI, by stage and sector.

reading.body:
Capital flowing into AI companies stands at 122 billion across 47 entities, with funding activity essentially flat over the past two weeks.

The stability in these numbers obscures what would normally be significant volatility in venture funding. A range of only four billion dollars across twenty days, from 118 to 122, suggests either that funding has plateaued at a sustainable level or that the measurement captures a narrow window during a pause between larger rounds. The data does not distinguish between seed stage and late-stage capital, so it cannot show whether money is concentrating in infrastructure plays, which would matter for understanding where capital sees the binding constraint.

For AI scaling, funding location matters more than funding volume. Capital flowing to compute-adjacent infrastructure, power generation, or data center construction would signal investor belief in where the bottleneck sits. Capital flowing to model development or applications would signal the opposite. This dataset shows neither, only the aggregate total and the company count. A reader should know that 47 companies receiving 122 billion means some entities are receiving vastly more than others, but the distribution is not here.
